author: poofywoo
body:
Avicus Moderator Application 


Age:

15

Timezone:

Nzst 

Do you have Teamspeak?

Yes

Do you have Discord?

Yes - poofy#0085

Do you have access to a recording software?

Yes



CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION 


Do you have any experience as a moderator on other servers?


This would be my first time actually and professionally moderating on a platform. I was once  a senior moderator on very small UHC network, that was later merged with another UHC network. I have experience being professional on platforms such as discord, as I am a Stratus network referee. But technically no moderating experience. But experience with professionalism.


What is your biggest weakness and how will it affect your moderating?


My biggest weakness when moderating will probably be identifying harder to detect hacks or glitch abuse. I'm worried that I'll make the wrong decision/ ban the wrong player. Especially during scrim matches. I'm worried that players from the opposite team will require a moderator to spectate somebody from my team. This may result in abuse from players depending on my decision. However I believe with practice and time, I should be able to learn as I go with help from other experienced moderators in teams and difficult situations.


What qualities do you think a leader must have? Would you consider yourself a leader? Why/why not?


A leader must be able to remain calm in all situations and must remain neutral. No bias. A leader should be able to communicate clearly and clarify when asked. A leader must be stern but not to an extreme. I am currently the leader of an Avicus team and understand how leaders run and how organised they have to be. I understand how leaders have to operate and how they remain calm in stressful situations. Even if leaders do have problems, they can always talk to their peers.


What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?


I hope to be just like any other Moderator. However due to my Timezone not many moderators if not any will be online. My Timezone will be useful in terms of helping other players when other moderators cannot help. Another attribute could be my personality. I am willing to work with other players and help out any of them. I do not get salty or angry easily. This can help during really stressful situations. I do not have bias in terms of my team and other teams in terms of moderating.


What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?


At times the community will be toxic. A good moderator should be able to always remain calm and professional at all teams. Should not get salty or become bias towards decisions. I believe I have these skills because I understand how things run and what/not to say. I also believe that listening to the community will help when making decisions . However making sure to keep bias out of it. 


What in your opinion are the three main character traits a moderator must have when moderating?


In my opinion a moderator should have these three traits; professionalism, organisation and a calm work ethic. Professionalism because it is important to always act professional when discussing staff terms or to the community. This is a job and you should always be professional when acting under that position, otherwise it looks bad and gives off a vibe that you should not be a moderator, if you cannot act it. 


Organisation. I have learned that moderators have to record. This means that having good organisation can help when bans are being appealed . You can access the recording easily without fuss. By being organised you can create a better work and playing environment for both you and the player. When organising events it helps to be organised to ensure everything can be run smoothly. 


Lastly having a calm work ethic I believe is key to be a good moderator. The community can be toxic so by being calm, you can address the situation easily and remain professional. By being a moderator you have to work with others some being different to others. By being calm it allows everybody to cooperate and work clearly.


CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS


You notice a moderator giving out a lot of false bans. They almost always have insufficient evidence or sometimes no evidence and they don’t seem to care. You notice it but other staff members don’t. What would you do?


Notify a senior moderator/admin privately as soon as possible. Provided I am 100% sure that this moderator is not performing well. Although these situation both are not desired I will be doing the right thing.


You are in Teamspeak with a few other players and they begin talking quite disrespectfully about a particular staff member. You agree with what they’re saying to an extent, but the conversation starts to become racial and very disrespectful soon after. You are all in a nightclub channel where this is allowed. What would you do?


As this channel is the "Nightclub" where these things are allowed, it is the player's perfect right to say whatever they want, as this is the rules. However if I believe if it gets extremely out of hand and unnecessary, I will say things like "calm it down." This means that it's not technically interfering with the player's right, but it is enforcing that maybe they should stop.


You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confidential but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?


Private message them that this is not allowed, and can be considered as leaking staff info. 


Some senior staff members are in teamspeak joking around with each other. They are removing others ranks, creating certain channels and even harassing certain users. They don’t mean any harm but some players in the channel feel a bit angry that they are using their permissions the way they are. What would you do?


Remind them casually that they are abusing their permissions and are affecting the players.


CRITERIA 3: OTHER

NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.



Why do you want to be a moderator?


Help out the players when other mods cannot be on. 


What does Avicus mean to you?


Avicus means a lot to me. I really love the competitive aspect and want to keep Avicus alive, in order to keep playing competitive. The community and staff are both really nice and I want to work with them.


Anything specific the staff team could do better? 


No. Maybe clarify their decisions. For example the Zaoki incident. I think the official team should have said what happened instantly.


Why did you choose to apply at Avicus?


Because it's the server with the best community. Everybody is nice and I want to do my part


Do you have anything else to add to your application?


I really hope to get accepted. I want to improve this network and help out players. I want to meet new people and get to know everybody a lot better.


If you have any questions, feel free to notify me!


Thanks 


- Poofywoo.
